relationship_definitions.exact: Equivalent classification for initial routing only; never identical fields, evidence requirements, adapter behavior or authority.
relationship_definitions.partial: One classification covers only part of the other; unrepresented aspects remain explicit and require question-level applicability review.
relationship_definitions.overlap: Classes intersect for some purposes but neither substitutes for the other; a selected product and evidence scope must resolve the intersection.
relationship_definitions.unmapped: No dedicated matching questionnaire classification exists in this snapshot; generic questions or related products do not close the gap.

rules: Resolve by explicit stable IDs and mapping revisions, never by catalog order, numeric suffix or display name.
Retain both original identifiers; a mapping never renumbers a source profile or replaces a runtime family ID.
One RFI may relate to multiple runtime families and multiple RFIs may relate to one family.
Mappings identify candidate routing and question applicability, not deployed products, authorized collection or enterprise completeness.
Bind the selected crosswalk revision into assignment/export/import/report lineage; later revisions cannot silently remap historical answers.
Unresolved aspects require an explicit applicability decision or documented limitation, not automatic copying of answers into another class.
No mapping creates a source instance, evidence source, assessed deployment, cryptographic use or admitted observation.

rfi_profiles.label: Application, business-service and configuration-item portfolio

mappings.rationale: Configuration-item and service records form one part of the combined portfolio questionnaire.
Application lifecycle and business-service ownership form another part; the portfolio is not assumed to be the CMDB.

unresolved_aspects: Confirm per-fact authority where separate application, service and configuration repositories overlap.

rfi_profiles.label: PKI, certification authorities and certificate lifecycle

mappings.rationale: Certificate inventory and lifecycle are one part of the combined PKI questionnaire.
Issuance hierarchy and trust sources need their own evidence route, potentially separate from lifecycle inventory.

unresolved_aspects: A certificate inventory does not establish certificate deployment or relying-party trust.

rfi_profiles.label: TLS termination, load balancing, proxies, API gateways and ingress

mappings.rationale: Listener and TLS termination configuration are part of this broader questionnaire.
API and ingress TLS overlap; workload identity and internal mesh policy also require the dedicated workload questions.

unresolved_aspects: Do not infer negotiated behavior from configured TLS settings or infer all mesh coverage from edge ingress.

rfi_profiles.label: Network device, controller, firewall, router and appliance configuration

mappings.rationale: Some device configurations expose TLS termination; the family is not a general network-device inventory.
Device management may include SSH endpoints but does not represent every device cryptographic function.
Device tunnels and VPN profiles intersect the VPN family, not the entire network configuration class.

unresolved_aspects: No dedicated general network-device configuration family exists in runtime v1.
Network telemetry is observed behavior, not a substitute for authoritative device configuration.

rfi_profiles.label: SSH, privileged access, bastions and machine identities

mappings.rationale: SSH is the directly applicable runtime portion; privileged-access and broader machine-identity functions are not implied.

unresolved_aspects: PAM approvals, session controls and non-SSH machine identities need explicit product-specific questions.

rfi_profiles.label: VPN, IPsec, IKE and remote access

mappings.rationale: Both classify VPN gateways, encrypted network access and peer dependencies for initial routing.

rfi_profiles.label: Source-code repositories and repository catalogs

mappings.rationale: Repositories supply the source part of the combined source-and-build runtime family; build and release require RFI-009.

unresolved_aspects: Source revision alone does not prove the runtime dependency or deployed artifact.

rfi_profiles.label: SAST, SCA, SBOM, code search and software-analysis results

mappings.rationale: Both classify software component, dependency and cryptographic call-site analysis sources.

rfi_profiles.label: CI/CD, build, release, package, container and artifact registries

mappings.rationale: Build and release metadata supply the build portion of the combined runtime family; source scope remains separately attributed.
Build pipelines may record signing steps and artifacts but do not necessarily own signing policy, custody or verifier populations.

unresolved_aspects: Artifact registry membership is not proof that a specific artifact was deployed or successfully verified.

rfi_profiles.label: Software, container, code and document signing services

mappings.rationale: Artifact signing is directly represented; document-specific signing and recipient policy may be outside this runtime family.
Document signing intersects communications, while artifact update paths remain in software-signing.

unresolved_aspects: Document-signing questions must remain applicable to the document service rather than copied to every software build.

rfi_profiles.label: Cloud resource inventories and cloud-native cryptographic services

mappings.rationale: Cloud resource and workload identity are the inventory portion of the questionnaire.
Cloud inventories may link KMS resources, but key-consumer and policy evidence requires the selected KMS interface.
Cloud secret-resource metadata can identify a route without proving rotation, consumers or handling policy.

unresolved_aspects: A cloud control-plane inventory is not automatically authoritative for every cryptographic service or workload it lists.

rfi_profiles.label: Key-management services and envelope encryption

mappings.rationale: Both classify KMS metadata, algorithms and key-consumer dependencies for routing.

rfi_profiles.label: General HSMs and enterprise cryptographic services

mappings.rationale: Both classify general hardware cryptographic modules, mechanisms and non-secret custody metadata.

rfi_profiles.label: Secrets management and application-secret references

mappings.rationale: Both classify secret and credential metadata, consumers and rotation references; no secret values are requested.

rfi_profiles.label: Identity providers, federation, tokens and assertion signing

mappings.rationale: Both classify issuer metadata, federation trust and token or credential consumers.

rfi_profiles.label: Workload identity, service meshes, container platforms and cluster ingress

mappings.rationale: Mesh routes and transport policy are a directly represented subset of the broader workload and container questionnaire.
Runtime workload and deployment inventory overlaps; a container platform is not necessarily a public-cloud resource source.
Workload identity intersects IAM, but mesh trust domains must not be equated with enterprise federation automatically.

unresolved_aspects: Cluster and container-platform inventory may need a qualified product mapping beyond the mesh or cloud subset.

rfi_profiles.label: Database, storage, filesystem and data-platform encryption

mappings.rationale: Databases and data platforms are one part of the combined data-protection questionnaire.
Storage and filesystem encryption overlap, while backup, archive and restore have separate RFI-018 questions.

unresolved_aspects: Database encryption settings do not establish backup encryption, retained-copy coverage or restoration success.

rfi_profiles.label: Backup, archive, tape and recovery-copy management

mappings.rationale: Backup and archive evidence supply part of the broader storage-and-backup runtime family.

unresolved_aspects: Backup metadata and restoration verification require distinct evidence bases.

rfi_profiles.label: DNS and DNSSEC management

mappings.rationale: DNS and DNSSEC are one portion of the combined DNS, email and document runtime family.

unresolved_aspects: Do not ask a DNS responder to attest to email or document systems; preserve DNS-specific rollover and delegation questions.

rfi_profiles.label: Email, message and document encryption or signing

mappings.rationale: Message and document protection provide another portion of communications; DNS remains separately scoped.

unresolved_aspects: Email, message and document products may have different owners, evidence routes and recipient populations.

rfi_profiles.label: Endpoint, server, configuration-management and operating-system inventory

mappings.rationale: Fleet versions, updates and trust configuration are represented; server runtime and configuration details can exceed the family model.
Host inventory may provide SSH configuration but cannot replace host-key, client-cohort and authenticated operation evidence.
Installed runtime/library inventory intersects dependency analysis, not every source-level cryptographic call site.

unresolved_aspects: Server, mobile and managed endpoint populations require explicit scopes rather than a shared completeness claim.

rfi_profiles.label: Devices, operational technology, firmware, attestation and secure boot

mappings.rationale: Both classify device and firmware trust chains, update constraints and operational-system evidence.

rfi_profiles.label: Payment, PIN, EMV, card-network and payment-HSM cryptography

mappings.rationale: Regulated payment cryptography is a specific part of the broader transaction runtime family.

unresolved_aspects: General HSM metadata does not satisfy payment-specific handling, ceremony or ecosystem requirements.

rfi_profiles.label: Blockchain, distributed ledgers, wallets and digital-asset custody

mappings.rationale: Transaction signing and specialist controls intersect, but wallet, quorum, ledger and custody semantics are not a lossless fit.

unresolved_aspects: No dedicated digital-asset custody runtime family exists in v1.
Do not normalize wallet, ledger, quorum or recovery facts as generic payment facts without a separately versioned model and tests.

rfi_profiles.label: Security telemetry, NDR, SIEM, vulnerability and exposure management

mappings.rationale: Observed network handshakes and sensor limits are one part of the broader security telemetry questionnaire.
Detection and drift evidence overlap the runtime assurance family; vendor claims and sensor observations remain distinct evidence bases.

unresolved_aspects: SIEM events, vulnerability records and configuration compliance require explicit product schemas; the network family does not cover all security telemetry.

rfi_profiles.label: Data catalogs, classification, retention, privacy and records management

mappings.rationale: Both classify protected-information context, lifetime, lifecycle and system associations.

rfi_profiles.label: Third parties, vendors, products, SaaS and lifecycle inventories

mappings.rationale: Vendor support, capability and lifecycle claims are a portion of the combined assurance-and-detection runtime family.

unresolved_aspects: Vendor statements do not independently verify deployed capabilities or ongoing drift; contract and product qualification remain separate.

unmapped_runtime_families.reason: No dedicated mainframe source-system RFI appears in the 27-profile catalog. Generic HSM, application or product questions may assist routing but are not equivalent.
unmapped_runtime_families.next_action: Retain the runtime family and draft a reviewed, versioned mainframe questionnaire extension before claiming question-level coverage.

unmapped_runtime_families.reason: No dedicated governance, exception or work-coordination source-system RFI appears in the 27-profile catalog. Policy-related questions elsewhere do not define a complete source profile.
unmapped_runtime_families.next_action: Retain the runtime family and draft a reviewed, versioned policy/exception/work-coordination questionnaire extension; imports must not manufacture approvals.

limitations: This is a reviewed-by-code development proposal, not an owner-approved enterprise taxonomy or question-level equivalence assessment.
Twenty-seven questionnaires and twenty-seven runtime families do not form a one-to-one correspondence or imply enterprise completeness.
The classification-only snapshot excludes private answers, owners, contact routes, source instances, schedules, payloads and credentials.
Recognition or mapping cannot establish a qualified product adapter, source access, cryptographic behavior, report acceptance or migration authorization.
Question IDs, template versions, answer scope and expected evidence remain separately bound; common questions must not be multiplied mechanically across every linked family.
